title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is written upside down. It continues the previous page, which built a linear-algebra theory of crystals killed by p ("cristaux p-isés"), and now applies it to group schemes.

Setting. Take a crystal M on S_cris over an F_p-scheme S, with maps F: M^(p) → M and V: M → M^(p).
- The previous page attached to M a perfect crystalline complex Δ*(M) of amplitude [0,1], with H^0 ≅ H^1 ≅ M and with F, V satisfying FV = VF = 0.
- It also gave two exact triangles (I)_cris and (II)_cris relating Δ* and its Frobenius twist Δ*^(p) to the two-term complexes [M^(p) →F→ M] and [M →V→ M^(p)].
- The key point: there are Zariski perfect complexes l, l^! of amplitude [-1,0] and a triangle (III) on S_zar: l[-1] → Δ* → (l^!)^∨ →.
- Pulling back along φ: S_cris → S_zar recovers (I)_cris. Here φ^* is Frobenius pull-back from Zariski data, i.e. Δ*^(p) ≅ φ^*Δ*.
- This uses the fact that on a PD-thickening killed by p, Frobenius factors through S. So the Frobenius twist of a p-torsion crystal depends only on Zariski data on S.

This page states a programme for a group G/S over an arbitrary base (G presumably finite locally free, or truncated Barsotti-Tate, killed by p). Can one attach to G:
- (a) canonically, Dieudonné crystals on S_cris, both contravariant D*(G) and covariant D_*(G);
- (c) D*(G), a module of finite presentation (or locally free of finite type?) on S_cris, with F: D*(G)^(p) ⇄ D*(G) :V and FV = VF = 0 (killed by p);
- (b) the co-Lie complexes ℓ_G and ℓ_{G*} of G and of its Cartier dual on S, perfect of amplitude [-1,0], together with a map π: (ℓ_{G*})^∨ → ℓ_G, i.e. a pairing ℓ_{G*} ⊗^L ℓ_G → O_S;
- (d) an exact triangle on S_cris of the form φ^*(ℓ_{G*})^∨[-1] → φ^*(ℓ_G) → Δ*_cris(G) →, whose connecting map is φ^*(π) viewed as O_{S_cris} → φ^*(ℓ_G ⊗ ℓ_{G*}^∨). This triangle therefore determines Δ*_cris(G), with H^0(Δ*_cris(G)) = D*(G) and H^1(Δ*_cris(G)) ≅ D_*(G). So the derived object Δ* packages the contravariant and covariant crystals together, and its construction is given by a triangle;
- (e) the corresponding exact triangle on S_zar, (ℓ_{G*})^∨[-1] → ℓ_G → Δ*(G) →, with Δ*(G) = ε_*(Δ*_cris(G)).

In short, this is a derived Hodge-filtration description. For p-torsion G, the Dieudonné crystal (as the complex Δ*) would be the Frobenius pull-back of the cone of a Zariski-local pairing between the co-Lie complexes of G and G*. The crystalline object would thus be entirely determined by Zariski derived data plus Frobenius. The problem served is crystalline Dieudonné theory over arbitrary (non-smooth, non-perfect) bases, including non-BT finite flat groups killed by p. This is the programme announced in Grothendieck's ICM 1970 talk and the Montreal 1970 lectures.
errors: In (d), as transcribed, the middle term would have to be φ^*(ℓ_G), possibly Frobenius-twisted, not φ^*(ℓ_{G*}^). As written the arrows do not type-check with the boundary φ^*(π). The page is a sketch with question marks, not proofs.

Exactness and the existence of π for general finite flat G killed by p are only asked, not proved. That H^1(Δ*_cris) is the covariant D_*(G) (rather than a Frobenius twist of D*(G)) is asserted with '≃' and needs justification via Cartier duality.
The relations are written FV = 0, VF = 0, consistent with p-torsion crystals. They are not FV = p as the machine transcription suggests.

ideas.what: Contravariant and covariant Dieudonné crystals of a group G over an arbitrary base S in char p, carrying F and V
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline Dieudonné module D(G) = Ext^1_cris(G, O)
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (ICM Nice 1970); Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal 1974)

ideas.what: Co-Lie complexes ℓ_G, ℓ_{G*}, perfect of amplitude [-1,0], with a pairing ℓ_{G*} ⊗^L ℓ_G → O_S
ideas.modern_name: Co-Lie complex and duality for finite flat group schemes
ideas.where_published: Montreal lectures mention Lie/co-Lie data; the derived pairing is not seen there

ideas.what: Derived Hodge filtration: an exact triangle ℓ_G-type → Dieudonné complex → (ℓ_{G*})^∨-type, on S_zar and, after Frobenius pull-back φ^*, on S_cris
ideas.modern_name: Hodge filtration of the Dieudonné crystal (derived form); F-zips / truncated displays

ideas.what: A two-degree complex Δ*_cris(G) with H^0 = D*(G) and H^1 ≅ D_*(G), packaging the contravariant and covariant crystals of a p-torsion group, determined as a cone
ideas.modern_name: Derived Dieudonné complex (cf. RHom(G, O_cris) with its two cohomologies; F-gauges)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot–Breen–Messing (Ext-complexes), later prismatic/F-gauge approaches (Anschütz–Le Bras, Mondal, Bhatt–Lurie)

ideas.what: The Frobenius twist of a p-torsion crystal is the pull-back of Zariski data via φ: S_cris → S_zar
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius factors through S on PD-thickenings killed by p; F-zips / Frobenius descent

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes that, for a group G killed by p over an arbitrary base, the crystalline Dieudonné object (as a complex Δ*_cris with H^0 = D*, H^1 = D_*) is the Frobenius pull-back of the cone of a Zariski-local pairing ℓ_{G*} ⊗^L ℓ_G → O_S between derived co-Lie complexes. This would make crystalline data for BT_1 and finite flat p-groups determined by derived Hodge data plus Frobenius.
missed.quote: i.e. un hom ℓ_{G*} ⊗^L ℓ_G → O_S ... Un triangle exact sur S_cris ... (qui détermine donc Δ*_cris(G))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates, in derived form and for non-smooth finite flat groups, the F-zip / truncated-display philosophy (Moonen–Wedhorn, Lau). It also prefigures recent work describing BT_1 and finite flat groups via derived Hodge data and F-gauges (Drinfeld's conjectures; Gardner–Madapusi). The derived version for arbitrary finite flat groups killed by p, using Illusie's co-Lie complexes, does not seem to be written in this explicit form.

deep.surprise_reason: The broad programme (Dieudonné crystals over arbitrary bases) is Grothendieck's known 1970 programme. The specific mechanism is a derived perfect complex packaging covariant and contravariant crystals, determined Zariski-locally by a pairing of co-Lie complexes after Frobenius pull-back. It is an unpublished and fairly modern-looking anticipation of F-zips and derived Hodge/F-gauge descriptions. It is only sketched, with question marks.
transcription_corrections: The page is upside down. Labels read a), c), b), d), e) in that order on the page.
Symbols in d) and e) are Δ* (∇-like triangle symbol): 'Δ*_cris(G)' and 'Δ*(G) = ε_*(Δ*_cris(G))', not D*.
Relations appear to be 'FV = 0, VF = 0', not 'FV = p, VF = 0'.
Margin diagram: S_cris →φ→ S_zar together with ε, labelled near d).
'(loc. libre de type fini ?)' is written near the S_cris brace in a).
